evidence: The reviewer cites server.ts:423-431 rejecting non-hello frames while pending-hello, and the hunk shows transmit() gated only on the socket being OPEN; the agent agreed ("Real bug") and gated transmit on currentState === "ready" with a regression test, despite the lexical pushback hint. Using the client's own handshake state rather than ws.readyState as the gate is a fair one-source-of-truth argument.
guidance_note: When refactoring a send path, enumerate every client state in which the send can be reached (connecting, open-before-welcome, ready) and state which ones are allowed to emit frames before writing the gate.

evidence: The hunk shows close() only calls ws.close() when readyState is OPEN yet finalizes and clears this.ws, so a CONNECTING socket's later open/message events could revive a closed client; the agent closed unconditionally and added per-socket `this.ws !== ws` guards plus a test. The stale-listener guard is about event identity, not a duplicated source of truth, so the law token is decoration.
guidance_note: When close() finalizes state inline, list every socket readyState close() can be called in and confirm listeners from a disowned socket cannot mutate the client.

evidence: The test awaits `setTimeout(r, 5)` then asserts `hub.sockets.length === 2`, a timing guess; the agent replaced it with a deadline-bounded poll. Flag is a false positive: ac590d0 only reformats the close addEventListener call, and the fixed sleep was in the test as originally submitted (it appears in the round-0 test file).
guidance_note: When a repo already has a poll-until-deadline helper pattern (connection-state.test.ts), use it for every timer-driven assertion in new tests instead of a fixed sleep.

evidence: transmit() wraps ws.send in try/catch and never throws, so the flushOutbox comment "A throw breaks the loop" is false; the agent rewrote it. Flag is a false positive for ac590d0 (formatting only); the packet does not include c8ad50b's diff, so whether the F1 fix introduced the try/catch that made the comment stale cannot be determined here.
guidance_note: When writing a how-comment about loop exit, check it against the callee's actual throw behavior in the same diff.

evidence: Round 3 reviewed the same commit ac590d0 as round 2 and repeated F4 verbatim; the agent pointed to 777c300 where the comment was already rewritten. The flag is a false positive: it is a duplicate re-review of a stale snapshot, not a consequence of any fix.
Duplicate of F3 raised against the same ac590d0 snapshot; the agent cites 777c300's poll loop bounded by `Date.now() + 100`. Not fix-caused; the reviewer re-reviewed an old head.

narrative: Round 0 found two real lifecycle bugs (calls sent before welcome, CONNECTING socket revived after close) and the agent fixed both with tests; round 1 was clean. A formatting-only push four days later (ac590d0) triggered round 2, which flagged a pre-existing fixed sleep and a stale comment, and round 3 re-reviewed the same commit and repeated both. No finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: Pushing a formatting-only commit on an otherwise-clean PR bought two extra review rounds of pre-existing nits; batch cosmetic changes with substantive ones or land them before review.
Law tokens were attached to every reply, including a stale-comment fix and a stale-listener guard where one-source-of-truth does not describe the defect.

evidence: The sentinel `let socketName = ""` is set once per describe, so after the first test a beforeEach that throws before reassignment leaves the previous name and the guard passes; the agent added `socketName = ""` after killServer in each afterEach (8b3accd).
guidance_note: When introducing a sentinel guard in per-test hooks, ask whether the sentinel holds at the start of every test, not just the first.

evidence: Same stale-sentinel gap in pane-stream.test.ts; 8b3accd adds `socket = ""` at the end of afterEach.

8b3accd touches three describe blocks in client.test.ts (lines 115, 218, 343) and the agent's F1 reply claims "all three describe blocks", but the file has a fourth ("Notification coverage (SPEC §23)") still calling killServer(socketName) unguarded. Both the original PR and the F1 fix missed it.
guidance_note: Before claiming a pattern is applied file-wide, grep for every call site (here `killServer(`) and count matches against the blocks edited.

narrative: A small test-hardening PR guarding killServer with a sentinel. Round 0 correctly noted the sentinel only held for the first test; the fix added per-test resets but, like the original PR, skipped the file's fourth describe block, which round 1 flagged. Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The PR's whole purpose was to harden every killServer call, yet neither the original change nor the fix enumerated call sites by grep; one search would have saved a round.

evidence: applySeed now passes a scrollToBottom callback to terminal.write, changing the call shape; the agent found the xterm-sink tests were outside the root vitest glob and two were genuinely failing, then updated them and added buffering tests.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR that changes a package's internals, run that package's own test suite directly rather than trusting the root CI glob to cover it.

evidence: The hunk strips a trailing "" capture line to fix an off-by-one with no test pinning it; the agent added a regression test asserting the seed is exactly "row-0\r\nrow-1".
guidance_note: Ship a bug fix with a regression test that pins the exact output shape that was wrong.

evidence: seed() buffers into pendingSeed until the first-resize rAF while write() goes straight to xterm, so PaneStream's synchronous post-seed drain lands live bytes before the seed; the agent confirmed the drain behavior and added a pendingWrites buffer flushed after applySeed.
guidance_note: When deferring one sink operation, check every other operation on the same ordering contract (seed before write) and defer them together.

narrative: A single review round found three real issues: stale test mocks (which exposed tests excluded from CI), a missing regression test, and a seed/write ordering break introduced by the new seed buffering. All were fixed in one commit, with no further rounds.
guidance_observations: The ordering bug in F3 was introduced by the PR itself; deferring seed() without deferring write() breaks the documented TerminalSink contract, which a check of the contract would have caught before review.

evidence: typecheck:tests runs tsconfig.e2e.json, whose specs resolve the package via dist .d.ts, so standalone use fails on a clean checkout; the agent moved the e2e check into `typecheck` after `tsc --build`, keeping typecheck:tests build-free.
guidance_note: When adding a check to a script, confirm the script's prerequisites still hold when it runs standalone.

evidence: The PR itself replaced typed stubs with `{ on, off } as unknown as TmuxClientLike`, which hides interface drift in a PR whose stated goal is gating tests against library types; the agent switched to FakeTmuxClient.
guidance_note: In a PR that adds a typecheck gate, do not silence the errors it surfaces with `as unknown as`; reach for the existing full fake first.

evidence: The agent does not dispute that runtime globals are off or that the tests import describe/it/expect explicitly; its rebuttal is that the root config does the same, which is an argument for fixing both, and its claim that vitest/globals is needed for "assertion-function resolution from the existing imports" is unsupported, since explicit imports carry their own types.
guidance_note: When setting `types` in a typecheck config, match the runtime config (vitest globals off means no vitest/globals) rather than copying a sibling config.

evidence: Same `as unknown as TmuxClientLike` cast introduced by this PR at a different call site; replaced with FakeTmuxClient.
Same PR-introduced cast at the detached-target test; replaced with FakeTmuxClient.
Same PR-introduced cast at the sequential-dispatch test; replaced with FakeTmuxClient.
Same PR-introduced cast at the unregister-mid-sweep test; replaced with FakeTmuxClient.
The hunk shows a previously typed `ReseedSchedulerClient` stub rewritten as a partial object cast through unknown; the agent replaced it with FakeTmuxClient plus vi.spyOn(client, "on").
Same PR-introduced cast in the getScheduler idempotency test; replaced with FakeTmuxClient plus a spy.

The F9 fix introduced `vi.spyOn(client, "on")` with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` as the last test statement, which is skipped on assertion failure; the leak is overstated, though, because the spy sits on a FakeTmuxClient created inside that test and no later test touches it. Moving restore to afterEach is cheap and correct.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces spies, put their restore in afterEach in the same commit instead of at the end of the test body.

evidence: Same end-of-body restoreAllMocks pattern, introduced by the F8 fix in the "subscribes to 'reconnected' exactly once" test; the spy is on a per-test local client, so cross-test leakage is limited, but afterEach cleanup is the correct structure.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces spies, put their restore in afterEach in the same commit instead of at the end of the test body.

evidence: The new tsconfig comment says the root tsconfig.tests.json "omits DOM", but with no `lib` set TypeScript's default lib includes DOM; the agent conceded and rewrote the comment. The comment was in the original PR (round-0 hunk), so this is not fix-caused.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that asserts another config's behavior, open that config and check the claim.

narrative: A PR adding typecheck gates for pane-terminal and e2e tests silenced the errors it surfaced with `as unknown as TmuxClientLike` casts, and round 0 flagged seven of them along with a build-order issue and a vitest/globals mismatch, which the agent wrongly pushed back on. The cast fixes introduced spies with end-of-body restore, which round 1 flagged twice alongside a pre-existing false comment. Round 1 would have happened anyway because of F12, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: The PR defeated its own goal: it was meant to make tests track library types, and it used double casts to get them past the new gate.
The one pushback rested on consistency with an equally flawed sibling config rather than on whether the claim was true.

evidence: The hunk guards only `f[0] !== ""`; `Number("")` is 0 and passes Number.isInteger, so "5;" yields row 0. The agent added the symmetric f[1] check.
guidance_note: When validating a multi-field parse, apply each guard to every field in the set, not only the first.

evidence: The preamble emits ?1049h for alternate_on=1 and nothing for 0, so a reused terminal in the alt screen stays there; the agent correctly notes ?1049l restores a saved cursor rather than homing, so the reviewer's symmetric fix would misplace the first row. It filed tmux-pane-terminal-u6a instead of changing code in this PR.

The claim that `out +=` in a loop is "quadratic-ish" does not hold in V8, where repeated concatenation builds ropes and flattens once; the agent accepted it and then enshrined the false rationale as a code comment ("repeated string concatenation is quadratic-ish for large pastes").
guidance_note: Check a performance claim against the runtime's actual string model before accepting it, and never copy an unverified reviewer rationale into a code comment.

evidence: `send-keys -H -t <target> ` with zero hex args is the original PR's output for empty keys, which tmux rejects; the agent short-circuited empty input in both TmuxClient.sendKeys and PaneStream.sendKeys, leaving the exported encoder still able to emit the malformed command (see F6).
guidance_note: When a wire-format builder has an input with no valid encoding, enforce the precondition in the builder that owns the format, not in each caller.

evidence: The agent confirms the websocket transport and server still UTF-8-decode frames while decodeOctalEscapes now assumes a Latin-1 container, and it deferred the fix to epic tmux-byte-codec-xxj; whether this PR regressed a path that previously worked, or the path was already broken, is not shown in the packet.
guidance_note: When a PR changes an input contract (here Latin-1 byte container), grep for every producer of that input and either convert them all or list them before review.

evidence: The F4 fix guarded the two callers but left the exported protocol-level sendKeys emitting `send-keys -H` with no args for ""; the agent moved the precondition into the encoder as a `string | null` return with an encoder test.
guidance_note: When fixing an invalid-output case, put the guard in the function that produces the output and has external callers, so every caller is covered.

evidence: The agent agrees CommandResponse.output is now a Latin-1 byte container, so non-ASCII window or session names arrive undecoded, a silent public-API change made by this PR, and it deferred even the documentation to ticket .4. Documenting the contract does not depend on the future codec helper, so the PR shipped the behavior change undocumented.
guidance_note: When a PR changes what a public field contains, document the new contract on that field in the same PR, even if the helper that eases migration comes later.

evidence: Idle global pointermove/pointerup listeners while collapsed are real but low-cost (handlers early-return on draggingRef); the agent rejected the collapsed-flag gate and scoped listeners to the drag's lifetime instead. NavbarResizer arrived in a mid-review commit (file count 18 to 20 at round 2), not from a finding's fix.

UTF-8-decoding raw seed bytes in a test sink is lossy for 0x80-0xFF, though only for test readability; accepting was reasonable, but the agent replaced the decoded text with `captured.byteLength > 0`, dropping the human-readable content assertions instead of using the Latin-1 decode the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags a lossy decode in a test, keep the assertion's strength by switching to a lossless decode rather than weakening to a non-empty check.

evidence: The test comment already says "the final row carries the mode epilogue", which explains why slice(2,7) checks only five blanks, so the mismatch was overstated; adding an explicit row-7 assertion still tightens the 8-row invariant.

The seed() doc says the bytes, including mode-restore escapes, are "exactly as tmux produced them", but parseSeedState synthesizes those escapes from display-message state; the agent reworded the doc to separate captured grid bytes from injected escapes.
guidance_note: When documenting a payload assembled from several sources, name each source's contribution instead of attributing the whole to one.

evidence: The F6 fix made sendKeys return null for "" but left the module-level note "Every function builds a string and appends LF. No conditional paths" in place; 5a0ea06 rewrites that note to name sendKeys as the exception.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a function's return shape, grep the module for file-level invariant comments that the change now contradicts.

evidence: The flag's commit 5a0ea06 only edits an encoder comment; the finding is on the per-drag listener code the F8 fix wrote, which listens for pointerup but not pointercancel. The pre-fix code had the same pointerup-only gap, so the fix carried it over rather than breaking something; the agent added a pointercancel handler.
guidance_note: When rewriting a pointer-drag lifecycle, enumerate every way a drag terminates (pointerup, pointercancel, unmount, a second pointerdown) before writing the teardown.

evidence: The historyLines default of 2000 was part of the original PR (round-0 summary: "default scrollback seeding to 2000 lines"), and the agent quotes the option's own doc stating the trade-off and the `historyLines: 0` opt-out, with the package pre-1.0. The flag is a false positive: 5a0ea06 only touched an encoder comment.

mode() returns offSeq for any non-"1" value including "", so an unexpanded format forces modes off, while pane_height/history_size treat "" as absent; the agent made "" a no-op. The flag is a false positive: e543972 only edits NavbarResizer.tsx, and mode() is original PR code.
guidance_note: When one parser treats empty fields as absent for some fields, apply the same rule to every field it parses.

evidence: F13's reviewer text explicitly suggested "calling any existing endDragRef.current at the start of a new drag"; e543972 added only the pointercancel listener and ignored that half, so the next round raised it separately. The stacking risk exists only because the F8 rewrite registers listeners per drag.
guidance_note: When a finding bundles several suggestions, answer each one on the thread, either implemented or declined with a reason, so none comes back as a separate finding.

narrative: A large byte-faithfulness PR ran ten rounds. Two fix chains drove repeat findings: the empty-sendKeys guard was first put in the callers (F4), then moved into the encoder (F6), then left a stale module comment (F12, the only finding of round 6); and a NavbarResizer change added mid-review (F8) was rewritten into per-drag listeners that missed pointercancel (F13) and the reviewer's own bundled suggestion about stacking (F16). Three cross-cutting issues (alt-screen reset, WS transport decoding, CommandResponse docs) were deferred to tickets, and one of those deferrals, the docs, was cheap enough to do in this PR.
guidance_observations: Adding unrelated example-app changes (NavbarResizer) mid-review opened a new surface that by itself produced three findings across three rounds.
Fixes landed one suggestion at a time; reading each finding for every suggestion it bundled (F13) and every owner of the invariant (F4) would have collapsed the two chains.
The agent accepted a false performance premise (F3) and wrote it into a code comment, the opposite failure from its well-argued pushback on F2 and F14.
